The Companies Act, 2013 s.138 uses mandatory wording, but only for prescribed classes of companies, and nothing in the sheet shows CRUT falls in a prescribed class. | EVIDENCE: Companies Act, 2013 s.138(1), in ALL-03 (human-verified): 'Such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed shall be required to appoint an internal auditor, who shall either be a chartered accountant or a cost accountant, or such other professional as may be decided by the Board to conduct internal audit of the functions and activities of the company.' Section 138(2): the Central Government 'may, by rules, prescribe the manner and the intervals in which the internal audit shall be conducted and reported to the Board.' CRUT-06 says CRUT is an SPV registered under the Companies Act, 2013 and created by H&UD notification No. 1919 dated 19-Jan-2018. It gives authorised and paid-up share capital of Rs 1 crore. CRUT-22 is only a listing page of H&UD rules, and none of the listed rules is a CRUT rule. | CAVEATS: The 'prescribed classes' are set in the Companies (Accounts) Rules, which are not in the sheet. Those rules, CRUT's turnover and borrowings, and its status as a public or private company are all unchecked. The H&UD notification 1919 (2018), CRUT's Memorandum and Articles, and any CRUT-specific internal audit provision are not in the readable sheet. | PERIOD: Companies Act as in force at the 31 Aug 2026 cut-off, per ALL-03 (consolidated text, date not stated). | LIMITS:

question: Is the parastatal mandated to prepare its financial statements or annual accouts within a specified timeline?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. No score is proposed. The sheet shows CRUT is a company registered under the Companies Act, 2013, but the passages I could read do not show a 'shall' deadline for preparing its annual accounts. | EVIDENCE: CRUT-06 says CRUT is an SPV created by the H&UD Department (Notification No. 1919 dated 19.01.2018, Corrigendum No. 7387 dated 19.03.2018) and 'registered under companies Act, 2013'. ALL-03 (Companies Act, 2013, human-verified) s.137(1) requires a copy of the financial statements 'duly adopted at the annual general meeting of the company, shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of annual general meeting'. That is a deadline for filing adopted statements, not for preparing them. ALL-03 s.129 (as shown on pages 86-88) and s.134 (page 91) appear in the excerpts only as fragments, without the preparation-timeline wording. ALL-03 s.394 and s.395 require a State Government to cause an annual report on a Government company to be prepared within three months of its AGM. That is a Government-level duty and not an accounts-preparation deadline. The s.96 AGM timing was not located in the retrieved text. | CAVEATS: The Companies Act sets time limits only indirectly, through the AGM and filing dates. Whether that counts as 'prepare within a specified time period' is an interpretation for the team. The constituting notification (No. 1919 of 2018) and CRUT's Articles of Association are not in the sheet as readable text. | PERIOD: Companies
quote: A copy of the financial statements, including consolidated financial statement, if any, along with all the documents which are required to be or attached to such financial statements under this Act, duly adopted at the annual general meeting of the company, shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of annual general meeting

Section 129(2) says the Board 'shall lay before' each AGM the financial statements for the financial year. Section 137(1) says the adopted statements 'shall be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of annual general meeting'. Both set deadlines only indirectly, through the AGM date. Neither sets an explicit deadline for preparing the accounts. The s.96 AGM timing (six months after year-end) was not in the text I read. A person must decide whether these indirect Companies Act timelines count as a 'specified time period' for preparing accounts. If they do, the mandatory 'shall' wording would support a 5. A person should also check CRUT's constituting notification (No. 1919 of 2018), its Articles of Association, and any Odisha rules for the missing text.
